stage_b_reviewed_content.statement:
Let $X$ be a ringed space. Assume that the underlying topological space
of $X$ has the following properties:
\begin{enumerate}
\item there exists a basis of quasi-compact open subsets, and
\item the intersection of any two quasi-compact opens is quasi-compact.
\end{enumerate}
Then for any directed system $(\mathcal{F}_i, \varphi_{ii'})$
of sheaves of $\mathcal{O}_X$-modules and for any quasi-compact open
$U \subset X$ the canonical map
$$
\colim_i H^q(U, \mathcal{F}_i)
\longrightarrow
H^q(U, \colim_i \mathcal{F}_i)
$$
is an isomorphism for every $q \geq 0$.
conclusions:

\longrightarrow

$$

reason: Proves degree-zero case on quasi-compact opens, dimension shifts through functorial injective embeddings and uses finite Cech coverings to establish vanishing for filtered colimits of injectives.

stage_b_reviewed_content.statement: Let $f:X\to Y$ be continuous, let $(\mathcal F_i)$ be a directed system of abelian sheaves on $X$, put $\mathcal F=\operatorname{colim}_i\mathcal F_i$, and fix $p\geq0$. If the opens $V\subseteq Y$ on which $\operatorname{colim}_i H^p(f^{-1}V,\mathcal F_i)\to H^p(f^{-1}V,\mathcal F)$ is an isomorphism form a basis for the topology of $Y$, then $\operatorname{colim}_iR^pf_*\mathcal F_i\to R^pf_*\mathcal F$ is an isomorphism of sheaves.
hypotheses:
Let $f : X \to Y$ be a continuous map of topological spaces.
Let $(\mathcal{F}_i, \varphi_{ii'})$ be a system of
abelian sheaves on $X$. Set $\mathcal{F} = \colim \mathcal{F}_i$.
Let $p \geq 0$ be an integer. Assume the set of opens $V \subset Y$ such that
$H^p(f^{-1}(V), \mathcal{F}) = \colim H^p(f^{-1}(V), \mathcal{F}_i)$
is a basis for the topology on $Y$.

reason: Uses sheafification commuting with colimits and agreement on a basis to deduce higher direct image colimit identification.
